sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: In lesson 1 you learned to tell things: I am ready, it is open. Now you will learn to ask and answer: «Is it possible?», «Yes», «No», «Where is he?», «What is it?». You will also learn the short way to say «not», the way people really talk.

examples.translation: You want to know his place.

blocks.text: The rule is the same as in lesson 1: not goes right after am, is or are. Now it works for everyone, not only I am: he is not, it is not, they are not.

sections.title: Short «not»: I'm not, it's not, they're not

blocks.text: When people talk, they almost always shorten the word before not: I am not → I'm not, it is not → it's not. That's how you answer quickly and calmly. The full form is also correct; it just sounds firmer.

examples.translation: I don't feel sure of myself.

drill.hint: One word is wrong. Tap it.
drill.fix: After I'm you need not, not no: I'm not convinced.

blocks.text: In many languages you ask a question just with your voice and keep the same order. In English the order changes: is moves to the front. It is possible → Is it possible? If you keep It is possible? and only raise your voice, it sounds like surprise, not a real question.

drill.prompt: You see two free seats. Ask your friend if they are near the stage.

sections.title: Which clip goes in the question

blocks.text: A question doesn't change who goes with which clip. I still takes am, he, she and it take is, you, we and they take are. Only the place changes: now the clip comes first.

drill.why: They always takes are, in questions too.

sections.title: Short answers: Yes, I am. No, it is not.

blocks.text: People usually don't repeat the whole sentence. They say yes or no, then who, then the clip: Yes, she is. You don't need to say the word from the question again.

examples.en: Are you well? Yes, I am.
Is she carsick? Yes, she is.
examples.translation: The car ride made her feel sick.

examples.en: Are they unpacked? No, they are not.
Is it broken? No, it is not.

blocks.text: A short «yes» never ends with a short form: Yes, I'm and Yes, she's are wrong. After Yes, use the full clip: Yes, I am. Yes, she is.

sections.title: They ask about you — answer about yourself

blocks.text: If someone asks Are you…?, they mean you. So in your answer you say I: Yes, I am. Yes, you are would sound like you're talking about them. Same with he and she: they ask Is he…?, you say Yes, he is.

examples.en: Are you well? Yes, I am.
Are you guilty? No, I am not.
Is he innocent? Yes, he is.

drill.question: Your friend asks: Are you well? You feel fine. What do you say?
drill.explain: They are asking about you, so you answer with I am: Yes, I am.

blocks.text: Yes and No answer the question itself. If someone asks Is it broken? and the lamp is just not plugged in, start with No and then say what's going on: No, it's unplugged. Yes would mean «yes, it's broken».

examples.en: Is it broken? No, it's unplugged.
examples.translation: It works, it just isn't plugged in.

examples.en: Is it valid? Yes, it is.
Is it bent? No, it is not.

fixes.wrong: Is it broken? — Yes, it's unplugged.
fixes.right: Is it broken? — No, it's unplugged.

blocks.text: Sometimes yes or no is not enough: you want to know who, what or where. Then the question word goes first, then the clip, then who: Where is he? Many languages say «He is where?», but in English the question word always starts the question.

examples.translation: One person isn't here. Which one?
You want to know his place.
You want to know their place.

drill.prompt: Your friend went out and didn't come back. Ask where he is.

sections.title: Don't mix up who, what and where

blocks.text: Who is for people. What is for things. Where is for places. Before you ask, think about what you don't know: the person, the thing or the place.

examples.translation: The thing is in front of you, but it's strange.
You know the thing, but you can't see it.

drill.why: The thing is in front of you, but you don't know what it is: What is it?

blocks.text: Later in the lesson there are lots of new words, but the trick is always the same. With each word you can say how it is, say it's not, and ask. Try it with any new word from the session.

examples.translation: Does he never change his mind?

blocks.text: Short forms like It's and He's don't start questions. The full clip goes first: Is it…?, Is he…?
Some of these phrases don't match other languages word for word. I am not interested, Is it shady?, It's overdue: learn them as whole phrases that you can use straight away.

examples.translation: It's late. The book must go back.

fixes.wrong: Are you well? — Yes, you are.

blocks.text: Almost every mistake in this lesson is about where the clip goes. In a question it comes first. After who, what or where it comes second. In a short «yes» it comes last, in full.

drill.question: You want to ask where your friend is. Which is correct?
drill.explain: The question word comes first, then is: Where is he?

blocks.text: To say «not»: not after the clip; when you talk, I'm not, it's not. To ask: put the clip first and keep it: Is it…? Short answers: Yes, I am or No, it is not. Who, what, where: the question word first, then the clip.

examples.translation: You want to know his place.
